title: Bobble-yoke pullover
excerpt: A top-down yoke pullover in aran yarn with a bobble-textured yoke section. The yoke is worked in rounds from the neck down, with bobble clusters formed from grouped fpdc to create a raised dot pattern. Graded XS to 3XL.
sourceNotes: Top-down yoke pullovers with bobble or textured yoke sections are a popular seamless garment construction.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cluster of five fpdc all worked into the same post, then closed together at the top. The grouped posts push outward to form a rounded bobble on the fabric surface. Used here across the yoke section only.

Regular increase rounds worked throughout the yoke section to add stitches evenly as the circumference expands from neck to underarm. Increases are placed at four fixed points to keep the yoke balanced.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 dc x 16 rows = 10 x 10 cm in aran on a 5 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Graded XS to 3XL. Size M: 100 cm bust.

content.text: Cast on at the neck and work the yoke in rounds. Begin
every other round at four points while simultaneously placing
at regular intervals across each non-increase round. Once the yoke reaches the underarm, split for sleeves and continue body in plain dc. Work sleeves separately in rounds with a dc cuff.
Size M: yoke depth approx 22 cm. Body circumference 100 cm. Body length 70.4 cm from underarm.
Chain 64 and join in round for neck. Work increase rounds every other round. Place bobble clusters on alternate rounds evenly spaced. Continue for approx 22 cm yoke depth.
Separate sleeves onto stitch holders. Work body in dc in round for the remaining body length. Work 3 cm dc hem.
Pick up sleeve stitches. Work in dc in round, decreasing slightly toward the cuff. Work 4 cm dc cuff.
The diamond cable vest uses fpdc panel work to build a single centred cable motif as the focal point.
